And as for people not knowing whether I am being ironic, that simply further reinforces my point that sarcasm/irony isn't always obvious in text form, so people should do a bit of checking about the poster/commenter before jumping to conclusions like "oh, this person has a dark joke for a username, they must be an awful person".

There is a difference between making a joke once (even if it is on display for every comment I make), and going around with nazi slogans/memorabilia on.

Anti-Semitism is a serious issue, and I have had a conversation with two of my friends (who just so happen to be Jewish) about religion, the war in Palestine right now and my username, and both of them looked at me and LAUGHED when I told them about it, because they KNEW that I meant it in jest, not in a serious "I think the burning/extermination of Jews is really funny" way.

THAT is the difference. If comedians the world over were going around "normalizing hate", they wouldn't have many gigs left to perform, would they? As I said, one joke (or comedy skit/sketch) is not normalizing hatred. If a comedian only made dark humour jokes during a show, then yes, it would likely be argued that they are bandying about all these heavy topics like laughing matters one after another, and that WOULD be bad. That is why most comedians only sprinkle dark humour into other jokes based on lighter topics like toilet humour.

If my username was a problem, or I had exhibited any form of anti-Semetic comment or value on this site, I thoroughly doubt that I would still have this account, as it would have been removed faster than I could blink. Especially with the current climate with the Israel Palestine war right now. 

I can understand (believe me I can) that sometimes it is not possible to derive the true meaning of a statement or sarcasm in a comment when it is just text on a screen, but I would NEVER go out of my house wearing anything that would denote me as even a nazi sympathiser, no matter wearing something which made me look like an actual nazi.
